question: Which of the following mountain ranges is home to the second-highest peak of the world, K2?
solution:
The correct answer is the** __Karakoram range.__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Karakoram range** is a mountain range in **China, India, Pakistan, Afghanistan and Tajikistan.**
 
• It is** highest peak K2(Godwin Austen or Qogir) **is located in the **Gilgit-Baltistan** region which Pakistan controls.
 
• The northernmost range of the Trans-Himalayan Ranges in India is the Great Karakoram Range** also known as the Krishnagiri range.**
 
• Karakoram Range extends **eastwards from the Pamir for about 800 km**. It is a range with lofty peaks [elevation 5,500 m and above]. It is the abode of some of the greatest glaciers of the world outside the polar regions.

 Ranges
 Features
 
 
 
 

 Ladakh Range
 
 
 
• It is located to the **north of Leh and is part of the Trans-Himalayan range,** which merges with the Kailash range in Tibet.
 
• **Khardung La and Digar La **are both passes located in this region.
 
• Ladakh's climate is known as a** "cold desert" **climate because of its arctic and desert characteristics.
 
 
 
 

 Pir Panjal Range
 
 
 
• The **PirPanjal Range **is a group of mountains in the Lesser Himalayan region, running from east-southeast (ESE) to west-northwest (WNW) across the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and the Pakistan-administered Kashmir.
 
• PirPanjal is the **largest range of the Lesser Himalayas.**
 
• The renowned Galyatmountains are also located in this range.
 
 
 
 

 Zanskar Range
 
 
 
• The Zaskar Range, sometimes called Zanskar, is a mountain range in the **Himalayas, south-central Asia, northern India, and China's western Tibet Autonomous Region.**
 
• It **divides Ladakh from the Kashmir lowlands and the Chenab River**.
 
• **Hanle River, Khurana River, Zanskar River, Suru River, and Shingo River** are among these rivers.
 
• The Zanskar Range is notable for the **Nanga Parbat (8126 m).**
